description: Cloud CRM and business platform with sales, service, marketing, commerce, and data products.
self_serve_details: A free Developer Edition org is documented for testing/development. API use requires the API Enabled permission and an OAuth client app configured within the org; this does not establish free production API access for every customer plan.
api_details: Official REST API supports create/manipulate/search of Salesforce records and access to query results, metadata, and other resources; Bulk, Metadata, and Connect REST APIs cover additional jobs. No endpoint count estimated.
mcp_details: First-party Salesforce DX MCP Server (beta) and Salesforce Hosted MCP Servers are listed in Salesforce developer documentation. These connect agents to an org/platform; this is distinct from a generic MCP wrapper.
blocker: Org-scoped OAuth/client-app setup and API permission; production access depends on the target org and plan.
buildability_rationale: A documented REST API, OAuth flow, free test/developer org path, and official MCP options make an integration technically feasible. Org-specific credentials/permissions and production edition access prevent treating it as universally frictionless.

description: Cloud communications platform with APIs for messaging, voice, and email.
self_serve_details: Twilio documents free-trial signup without a credit card after email and phone verification. Trial includes limited product units, a 30-day expiry, and account-status restrictions; paid upgrade is needed to remove trial limits.
api_details: Multi-product HTTP APIs and SDK/CLI support; official Twilio documentation describes a hosted docs MCP indexing public API specifications across products. API breadth is broad across communications products; no endpoint count is used in this record.
mcp_details: First-party hosted Twilio MCP at https://mcp.twilio.com/docs. It searches/retrieves API docs and schemas (read-only); it does not execute Twilio API operations and needs no Twilio credentials.
blocker: Trial unit, recipient, geographic, template, and expiry restrictions; production sending requires paid account/upgrade.
buildability_rationale: A documented HTTP API, API-key/Basic auth, and self-serve free trial make integration feasible. Trial limits are material for a live communications agent, and the first-party MCP is documentation-only rather than an execution server.

description: REST-based seller/vendor APIs for catalog, listings, pricing, orders, fulfillment, inventory, reporting and related selling operations.
self_serve_details: For a public app serving multiple sellers/vendors, official onboarding requires a developer profile review, approved roles and Amazon approval/listing for Selling Partner Appstore distribution. A private app for one organization follows a less public path; this distinction is material.
api_details: Official docs describe REST-based APIs across catalog/listings/pricing/orders/fulfillment/inventory, notifications and bulk operations; Data Kiosk supports GraphQL queries. Roles and access vary by operation.
mcp_details: No first-party MCP status assigned in the pilot first pass; targeted official-source MCP search is required before classifying absence.
blocker: Public developer profile/role approval and Amazon approval for public Appstore distribution; selling partners must separately authorize.
buildability_rationale: SP-API is broad and technically buildable, but a reusable public toolkit needs the approved public-developer/app route and role access. A private developer route is documented for one organization and does not remove the public distribution gate.

description: Developer platform for building, scaling, and delivering software with code hosting and collaboration workflows.
self_serve_details: Users can create personal access tokens themselves; GitHub recommends GitHub Apps for organization/on-behalf-of-user integrations. Token permissions, repository ownership, org policy, and SAML SSO can limit access or require approval.
api_details: Extensive versioned REST API documentation spans many resource families and supports integrations, data retrieval and automation; endpoint-specific token/permission requirements apply. No endpoint count used.
mcp_details: GitHub maintains the first-party github/github-mcp-server repository and hosted remote MCP server. It supports repository/code, issues/PRs and workflow tools, with PAT/OAuth/host-specific setup requirements.
blocker: Least-privilege token scopes/permissions, organization policy/approval, SAML SSO and app installation can limit access.
buildability_rationale: The documented REST API and official MCP server make an integration feasible now. Access is identity- and permission-bound; org-owned resources may require admin approval or installation and the MCP host/auth path varies.

description: AI meeting notetaker that transcribes meetings and turns conversations into searchable summaries, insights and action items.
self_serve_details: The official Public API is available for Enterprise workspaces; users create an API key in account Developer settings, and accounts without the feature are directed to their account manager. MCP is a separate OAuth connection; its plan-entitlement matrix was not stated in the inspected help page.
api_details: Documented REST endpoints cover channels, conversations, transcripts/audio, action items, insights, outlines and workspace data; workspace webhooks support event-triggered exports. Useful but confined to meeting/workspace data.
mcp_details: Official remote Otter MCP endpoint is https://mcp.otter.ai/mcp; OAuth-authenticated; documented tools include search, fetch and user info. Supported first-party setup paths include Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and others; account/platform support can vary.
blocker: Public API is Enterprise-only; MCP tools are a bounded search/fetch/user-info surface and MCP plan/host eligibility is not fully specified.
buildability_rationale: A first-party OAuth MCP path and documented public API exist, so some agent-callable functionality is feasible. Broad API access requires Enterprise workspace availability; MCP tool coverage and host support limit scope.
